title: Deepavali picnic in Malaysia turns tragic as flash floods hit Selangor - South China Morning Post
text:
Deepavali picnic in Malaysia turns tragic as flash floods hit Selangor | South China Morning Post Health & Environment - Health & Environment Deepavali picnic in Malaysia turns tragic as flash floods hit Selangor Advertisement Malaysia This Week in Asia Health & Environment Deepavali picnic in Malaysia turns tragic as flash floods hit Selangor 
 A local man died and seven foreigners went missing in the disaster, prompting evacuations and a review of flood mitigation work
 2 -MIN READ 2 -MIN Listen Joseph Sipalan in Kuala Lumpur Published: 1:08pm, 10 Nov 2026 Updated: 1:14pm, 10 Nov 2026 Flash floods during a Deepavali picnic in Malaysia have killed a man and left seven others missing, as authorities evacuated hundreds from flood-prone areas in Selangor and Perak states amid a strengthening monsoon season. The shifting monsoon winds also triggered a surge in thunderstorms across the country, helping clear out a months-long curtain of transboundary haze . Local officials said they found the body of the victim, identified as V. Vijayan, at around 1.30am on Tuesday at a bridge about 2.7km (1.6 miles) from the Sungai Pertak picnic site in Selangor. He was believed to have gathered there with a group a day before to celebrate the festival also known as Diwali.
